newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials have to delay Mir repairs.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials have to delay Mir repairs.

text.p: A computer failire on board the ailing Mir space station has sent the ship spinning chaotically in orbit, forcing engineers to shut off all but vital life support systems, Mission Control officials said.
"We have turned off all energy-consuming equipment and only left life support systems operational," flight director Vladimir Solovyov told reporters.
"With this computer fault today we are bracing ourselves for a tense situation with the battery buffers, our energy reserves."
Mir's computer failed a few minutes before it docked with a Progress resupply ship, forcing its commander to take manual control of the docking procedure.
Mir, which draws its energy from keeping its solar panels aimed at the sun, would probably stay disorientated until at least Tuesday morning. "It will be chaotically spinning," Solovyov said.
The problems meant vital repairs to Mir scheduled for Wednesday would have to be delayed. "Unfortunately we have to move back repairs by two or three days," he said.
The repairs are aimed at solving a major problem with Mir's energy supply which occurred after a docking procedure on June 25 almost identical to Monday's operation.

The June 25 docking led to a collision between the supply ship and Mir -- the worst accident in the history of the 11-year-old station. A string of other problems meant Mir was already crippled before Monday's computer failure.
